author: samuelgoodparty
title: Read a priority's answers through the MRP model instead of raking
body:
## Why

Raking answers to the census and checking a 10-point margin treats self-selected respondents as a random sample. Samuel decided that a priority's read should instead ask:

- whether every major group has been heard, with at least 3 answers each;
- how sure a model of each group's opinion is.

This PR keeps the results page exactly as it looks today (`docs/decisions/2026-10-19-civic-panel-two-rounds-coverage-sizing.md`, `docs/features/civic-panel-mrp.md`). Like Bryan's raked read, it sits behind `serve-citizen-panels` and replaces that read directly, with no second flag.

## What changes

- **Data reads.** Two new aggregate reads run against the same district table every contacts read uses:
  - the district's cells, used as the model's frame;
  - the coded answers (#2972) grouped by those same cells. Yes counts as 1, no as 0, mixed as 0.5, and not-an-answer is left out.
- **`mrpReadStatus` maps the model onto the existing contract:**
  - `tooEarly` while some major group has no answer;
  - `notYetRepresentative` under 3 answers in some group;
  - `gettingClose` while some group's 90% range is wider than 20 points;
  - otherwise `representative`.
- **What the page shows.**
  - "Hear from more" names the groups actually holding the read back.
  - `needed` is the number of answers still missing to give every group 3.
  - Representation bars are now unweighted.
- **Cleanup.** The raking code this replaces is removed.

## Follow-ups

- **"Parts not reached" can disagree with "hear from more".** `unreachedAreaFor` still uses the old tract-shortfall rule. When the model names that group but the old rule finds no tract, the existing "every part has answered" message shows. It fails gracefully, but the two should share one rule.
- **Scales are fixed.** The model uses default scales; learning them from past priorities needs one warehouse read per past priority.
- **Untested against the real warehouse.** The SQL is tested as strings only, and the model's speed on very large districts is unmeasured.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how civic-panel priority read status and `needed`/`underrepresented` are computed for all `serve-citizen-panels` users, with new Databricks SQL and caching; UI contract is unchanged but behavior diverges from the old raked rules.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Priority “good read” now comes from MRP on coded answers**, not census raking, still behind `serve-citizen-panels` and using the same `PriorityReadStatus` contract labels.
> 
> `PriorityResultsService` loads **`PriorityAnswer`** codes (yes/no/mixed averaged per person), builds model inputs via new warehouse aggregates **`buildDistrictCellsSql`** / **`buildAnswerCellsSql`** (`CensusCompositionSource.mrpInputs`, 15‑minute caches), fits with **`estimateMrp`**, and maps outcomes in **`mrpReadStatus`**: major groups (≥3% of district on age, tract, gender, race when nameable) need ≥3 coded answers; **`gettingClose`** when a group’s 90% range exceeds 20 points; **`needed`** counts answers still missing for every major group to reach 3; **`underrepresented`** uses **`batchTargets`** on groups holding the read back. Representation comparison bars are **unweighted**; raking/`priorityReadStatus`/`weighToCensus` and weighted representation are removed.
> 
> Docs, contracts comments, product copy, and tests are updated to match; **`isTargeted`** is exported for read-status targeting.
>

+    ` ${tractSql()} AS tract, ${raceSql()} AS race, count(*) AS people` +

+// person's yes rides in on the id list it shares with others of the same
+// value, so only the sums come back, never a person.
+export const buildAnswerCellsSql = (
+  district: DbxDistrict,
+  answers: PersonAnswer[],
+): DbxStatement => {
+  const bag = createBag()
+  const where = buildScopeSql(bag, {
+    district,
+    filters: filtersSchema.parse({
+      id: { in: answers.map(({ personId }) => personId) },
+    }),
+  })
+  const byYes = new Map<number, string[]>()

+    if (yes === 0) continue

+    ids.push(personId)

+        ` THEN CAST(${bag.bind(String(yes))} AS DOUBLE)`,

+  const yesSql = arms === '' ? '0.0' : `CASE${arms} ELSE 0.0 END`
+  const sql =
+    `SELECT ${ageBandSql()} AS age_band, ${genderSql()} AS gender,` +
+    ` ${tractSql()} AS tract, ${raceSql()} AS race,` +
+    ` sum(${yesSql}) AS yes, count(*) AS answers` +
+    ` FROM ${district.table} v ${where}` +
+    ' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4'

+group in the district has answered on it, pooled across texts, calls and
+doors, and a model of the coded answers is sure enough of each. gp-api
+decides it in one place, `mrpReadStatus`
+(`gp-api/src/priorities/util/mrpReadStatus.util.ts`), returning
+`{ answers, needed, good, status, underrepresented }`. A major group holds
+3% or more of the district on age band, tract, gender, or race when
+`raceNameable` holds (10 coded answers with a known race, 70% of all); the
+pooled `other` never counts.
+
+| `status`               | Rule                                                                                                     |
+| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `tooEarly`             | a major group has no coded answer                                                                        |
+| `notYetRepresentative` | a major group has fewer than 3                                                                           |
+| `gettingClose`         | a major group's 90% range is wider than 20 points                                                        |
+| `representative`       | none of the above; `good` is exactly this                                                                |
+| `enoughAnswers`        | the district could not be read and answers meet `answersNeeded`; `good`, but no claim about who answered |
+
+The model is MRP (`gp-api/src/priorities/util/mrp.util.ts`,
+`docs/features/civic-panel-mrp.md`): each person's coded answers to the
+priority (`PriorityAnswer`; yes 1, no 0, mixed half, not an answer left out,
+averaged when a person answered twice) fit by age band, gender, tract and
+race, reweighted to the district's own voter-file cells. Race is L2's
+modeled ethnicity folded as the panel's steering folds it
+(`docs/decisions/2026-10-19-race-ethnicity-in-civic-panel.md`); it shapes
+the model either way and counts as a group only when nameable. Scales are
+the model's defaults; nothing learns them from past priorities yet.
+`answers` is the people heard (the results page's count); `needed` is
+`answers` plus the fewest more that could give every major group 3 (the
+dimension furthest short), so "N more answers" counts what is missing.
+`underrepresented` names, in `batchTargets` order (`civicPanelAllocation.util.ts`),
+the one or two groups holding the read back: short of voices, or with a
+range still too wide; every tract reads as `unreachedAreas`

+read, `needed` is `answersNeeded(population)` from contracts for the census
+row's population (`CensusCompositionSource.population`, memoized per
+district; an unknown one uses the uncorrected 96), enough answers are a good
+read labeled "Enough answers", never "Representative", and fewer are too
+early. A read is kept in process for 15 minutes per priority and its coded
+answers (`PriorityResultsService`), so a new or recoded answer reads again
+and a failure is never kept. **The official never sees a share, a range or
